task: Remediate the high-severity sharp/librsvg CVE-2026-96889 dependency finding by moving the locked optional Next.js sharp chain from 0.35.4/libvips bundle 1.3.3 to the current patched 0.35.5/libvips bundle 1.3.4 without weakening npm audit or changing product behavior.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Exact-head CI now fails its non-bypassable production dependency audit because the lockfile installs sharp 0.35.4 with the vulnerable librsvg-bearing prebuilt dependency chain, while the supported patched sharp release is 0.35.5; this external security drift blocks Unit 3 even though Unit 3 itself does not alter dependencies.
observableOutcomes: package.json deterministically constrains the transitive Next.js sharp dependency to patched sharp 0.35.5 without changing Next.js, React or application runtime contracts.
package-lock.json resolves sharp and its platform/libvips optional packages to the exact 0.35.5 / 1.3.4 patched artifact family and npm ci remains deterministic.
The real exact-head Security Audit passes naturally with no advisory suppression, timeout increase, allowlist, or audit-level downgrade.
Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build remain green and Unit 3 can subsequently rebase/reconcile from the new main.
unresolvedRisks: Sharp is an optional transitive dependency of Next.js image optimization, so a broad npm update could unintentionally churn unrelated platform packages.
Native prebuilt package identity spans sharp plus @img/sharp-* and @img/sharp-libvips-* packages; updating only the top-level lock entry would create an inconsistent install graph.
Security advisory feeds are external to repository state, so a previously green commit can become release-blocked without source changes and must still fail closed.

in: Add an exact root override for sharp 0.35.5.
Regenerate/update only the lockfile dependency graph required by that override.
Extend the existing dependency-security contract regression to assert patched sharp/libvips identities.
Prove the real exact-head npm security audit plus normal quality/type/build gates.
out: No audit suppression, allowlist, severity downgrade or workflow change.
No Next.js, React, Supabase, product runtime, auth, commerce, database, Builder or storefront source change.
No broad dependency refresh beyond the sharp native/prebuilt dependency family required by the patched release.
No Unit 3 orchestration code changes on this security hotfix branch.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: A high-severity native image-processing dependency finding blocks release and can affect server-side processing of attacker-influenced image inputs. The remediation is small but changes the deterministic install graph and native binary family, so it requires exact versioning, bounded lockfile churn, real npm audit proof, and full build regression without weakening any security gate.

acceptanceCriteria: package.json pins sharp exactly to 0.35.5 through the existing overrides authority.
package-lock.json installs node_modules/sharp at 0.35.5 and the corresponding @img/sharp platform packages at 0.35.5.
package-lock.json installs the corresponding @img/sharp-libvips platform packages at 1.3.4.
No unrelated direct dependency version changes are introduced.
The exact-head npm security audit no longer reports GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w / CVE-2026-96889.
Full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build remain green.
invariants: Security audit enforcement remains unchanged and authoritative.
The fix removes the vulnerable installed dependency rather than hiding its finding.
Next.js remains pinned at 15.5.24 and application dependencies remain otherwise unchanged.
Only the sharp native/prebuilt package family may change as a transitive consequence of the exact override.

failureModes: Only package.json is changed and npm ci still installs vulnerable lock entries.
Only sharp top-level lock entry changes while platform-native/libvips package identities remain stale.
A broad npm update changes unrelated transitive dependencies and expands release risk.
The audit is silenced rather than the vulnerable dependency being removed.
A loose version range later resolves to an unreviewed native binary.
The patched native dependency family fails installation or Next.js production build.
edgeCases: Next.js declares sharp as an optional dependency with range ^0.34.3 || ^0.35.3, so exact 0.35.5 remains compatible.
The repository does not directly import sharp in package.json; the root override controls the transitive optional dependency.
Platform-specific @img packages are optional but are part of lockfile integrity across supported environments.
The advisory may not affect every image format equally, but the release gate treats the installed high-severity dependency as blocking.

alternatives.summary: Suppress or allowlist the new npm audit advisory.
alternatives.reason: This weakens the blocking security authority and leaves the vulnerable package installed.

alternatives.summary: Upgrade Next.js or the broader framework dependency set to obtain a newer sharp transitively.
alternatives.reason: Next.js 15.5.24 already accepts sharp 0.35.5; a framework upgrade would add unnecessary product/runtime scope.

alternatives.summary: Pin sharp exactly to 0.35.5 and update only its native/prebuilt lockfile family plus the existing dependency security regression.
alternatives.reason: This is the smallest deterministic remediation that removes the affected dependency while preserving existing framework and product contracts.

specialistReviews.finding: Exact-head npm audit reports high-severity CVE-2026-96889 through sharp 0.35.4 and does not classify the failure as transient network noise.
specialistReviews.resolution: Install the current patched sharp 0.35.5 dependency family; no audit exception or severity downgrade is allowed.

specialistReviews.finding: A normal npm update can rewrite a large optional native dependency graph and unintentionally change unrelated release inputs.
specialistReviews.resolution: Constrain the edit to an exact sharp override and accept lock churn only inside sharp/@img sharp native packages; full diff and Release Risk remain blocking.

specialistReviews.finding: Dependency manifests are already canonical DOMAIN-RELEASE inputs and do not require a new dependency authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: Reuse the existing dependency-contract subsystem, release-domain ownership and dependency-security regression instead of adding a new security subsystem.

challenge.scenario: The audit is made green by changing workflow flags.
challenge.finding: The vulnerable native dependency would remain installed.
challenge.resolution: Workflow files are out of scope; exact-head npm audit must pass unchanged.

challenge.scenario: Only package.json gets an override while the lockfile remains 0.35.4.
challenge.finding: npm ci uses lock authority and either rejects the mismatch or retains stale dependency identity.
challenge.resolution: package.json and package-lock.json form one coherent dependency transaction.

challenge.scenario: Only node_modules/sharp is bumped in the lockfile.
challenge.finding: Its exact @img/sharp and @img/sharp-libvips optional dependencies could remain inconsistent with the patched release.
challenge.resolution: The complete sharp-native family required by 0.35.5 is updated as one bounded lock graph.

challenge.scenario: A broad npm update refreshes unrelated packages.
challenge.finding: The hotfix becomes an uncontrolled dependency release.
challenge.resolution: Diff review and contract test require unchanged direct dependencies and bounded sharp-family churn.

challenge.finding: A future lock regeneration could silently select a later unreviewed native dependency version.
challenge.resolution: Pin the root override exactly to 0.35.5.

challenge.scenario: Patched sharp is incompatible with the current Next.js line.
challenge.finding: Production build or image optimization installation could regress.
challenge.resolution: Next.js current optional range includes ^0.35.3; exact-head npm ci, TypeScript and Production Build remain mandatory.

challenge.scenario: Unit 3 code is modified together with the security hotfix.
challenge.finding: The emergency dependency remediation would lose bounded scope and obscure proof attribution.
challenge.resolution: Security branch touches only plan, dependency manifests and the existing dependency security test; Unit 3 remains isolated until this hotfix merges.

proofPlan: Require Plan Before Code PASS on this plan-only security branch before dependency edits.
Pin sharp exactly to 0.35.5 and update only the corresponding sharp/@img native lockfile family.
Extend tests/dependency-security-contract.test.ts to assert exact sharp 0.35.5 and representative libvips 1.3.4 identities while preserving the source-map-js regression.
Run Edit-Time Guard and Incremental Replay.
Require unchanged Release Risk Budget PASS.
Require exact-head Security Audit PASS with no exception.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build, then Completion Truth and Lifecycle Closure before merge.

requirements.requirement: The deterministic dependency contract installs patched sharp 0.35.5 and corresponding libvips bundle 1.3.4 instead of the vulnerable sharp 0.35.4 chain, with unchanged audit enforcement.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The remediation must not disable, suppress, allowlist or downgrade the security audit.
The lockfile must not retain sharp 0.35.4 or its vulnerable libvips 1.3.3 package family.

requirements.requirement: The security remediation remains a bounded dependency-contract release under the unchanged Release Risk authority and does not expand into product runtime or unrelated dependency upgrades.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The remediation must not intentionally upgrade unrelated product or dependency subsystems.
